meta.name: Volt Analytics Tab — Allure-inspired data density on Volt brand
meta.description: Design DNA for a new 'Analytics' view inside FintechBankApp's WEB dashboard, fusing Allure Report's dark, data-dense reporting layout with the existing Volt brand (yellow/black, rounded cards, mobile-first bottom nav).
source_references: http://127.0.0.1:56784 (Allure Report - Overview, Graphs sections, screenshots captured live)
http://localhost:3000/dashboard (current Volt HomeView, screenshots captured live)

primary.role: brand accent, primary CTA, chart highlight (borrowed from Volt bottom-nav/buttons)

secondary.role: Allure-style dark surface background for the Analytics view only

accent.role: secondary chart series (purple, matches Allure's 'Unknown' status slice)

neutral.usage: Neutral scale reserved for Analytics tab chrome (cards, dividers, sidebar); rest of app keeps existing light/yellow neutrals

color.contrast_strategy: dark-on-light dominant inverted to light-on-dark inside Analytics; white/95% text on near-black cards, semantic colors carry all status meaning so it stays scannable at a glance

font_families.heading: existing app font (Inter/system-ui, unchanged)
font_families.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular (for numeric KPIs, matches Allure's tabular figures)

typography.font_style_notes: Keep Volt's existing geometric sans everywhere; do not introduce a new font family just for this tab

spacing.section_rhythm: 16px gap between cards, 24px between major sections — denser than Volt's current 20-24px card rhythm, matching Allure's tighter grid

layout.grid_system: 2-column card grid on desktop (matches Allure's Overview grid), collapses to 1-column stack under 768px

shape.border_usage: subtle 1px (rgba(255,255,255,0.06)) separating cards from dark background instead of shadow

elevation.shadow_style: soft diffused, low-intensity (dark theme relies on surface-color steps, not shadow, exactly like Allure)
elevation.depth_cues: color intensity (surface steps from #1A1D29 to #3A3F52) over heavy shadows

iconography.style: line icons, already Lucide in this codebase (per commit ef1ce7f8) — reuse, do not add a second icon set

motion.easing: ease-out for entrances, ease-in-out for hover
motion.entrance_pattern: fade + 8px slide-up per card, staggered ~40ms (matches motion/react already used in Dashboard.tsx)
motion.philosophy: minimal functional — motion signals state change (tab switch, data refresh), never decorative

components.button_style: reuse existing Volt pill buttons for actions inside this tab (e.g. 'Exportar', 'Periodo'); do not invent a new button style
components.input_style: reuse existing Volt input style for filters/date-range picker
components.card_style: dark surface card, 12-16px radius, 1px hairline border, no drop shadow, 16-20px internal padding — new pattern specific to this tab
components.navigation_pattern: secondary in-tab sub-nav (pills or underline tabs: Visao Geral / Categorias / Tendencia / Faturas) sitting below the existing BottomNavBar — does not replace it
components.modal_style: reuse existing Volt modal component for any drill-down detail view
components.component_notes: New primitives needed: DonutStatusCard, TrendLineCard, CategoryBarCard, HistogramCard, ProgressBarRow — all dark-surface, all consuming a shared `ChartCard` shell wrapper

aesthetic.visual_metaphor: a control room panel — glanceable status at a glance, drill down on demand
aesthetic.era_influence: 2020s dark-mode SaaS analytics (Allure, Grafana, Vercel dashboard)

visual_language.whitespace_usage: tight but not cramped — breathing room comes from consistent 16px gaps, not empty space
visual_language.visual_weight_distribution: even grid weight, one hero KPI card (balance/health donut) gets 2x visual size like Allure's Status card
visual_language.focal_strategy: single hero element (top-left status/health donut) + distributed supporting cards
visual_language.contrast_level: high (light text/charts on near-black surfaces, semantic colors pop hard)
visual_language.texture_usage: flat color only, no gradients or noise

composition.hierarchy_method: scale contrast + color weight (hero card larger + brand-yellow accent draws eye first)
composition.balance_type: asymmetric (2-col grid, hero card spans differently than Allure's since mobile-first reflow is required)
composition.flow_direction: top-to-bottom, left-to-right reading of cards, same as Allure Overview
composition.grouping_strategy: related metrics clustered in one card (e.g. entradas/saidas/resultado together, like current FinancialHealthModal already does)
composition.negative_space_role: separates card clusters, not used for drama

imagery.photo_treatment: none — this is a data view, no photography
imagery.graphic_elements: charts only (donut, line, bar, histogram, progress bar) — no decorative shapes

interaction_feel.feedback_style: immediate hover highlight on chart segments/bars with tooltip, matching Allure's chart hover behavior
interaction_feel.hover_behavior: desktop: tooltip + slight brightness increase on hover; mobile: tap-to-reveal tooltip (no hover-only info, per mobile-principles)
interaction_feel.transition_personality: snappy, smooth glide — never bouncy (this is a finance app, not a game)
interaction_feel.loading_style: skeleton cards matching final card shapes, not spinners (keeps layout stable)
interaction_feel.microinteraction_density: low — this view is for scanning data quickly, not for delight-driven exploration

brand_voice_in_ui.formality: semi-formal (keeps Volt's friendly copy tone in labels, but numbers/charts stay clinical)
brand_voice_in_ui.cta_style: subtle suggestion (e.g. 'Ver detalhes' link, not a loud button, since this is a read-mostly view)
brand_voice_in_ui.empty_state_approach: same pattern as Allure's 'There is nothing to show' — plain centered text, no illustration, no dead space drama
brand_voice_in_ui.error_tone: calm and actionable, consistent with existing Volt error states

overview.fallback_strategy: reduce to CSS — charts degrade to plain numbers/table if a chart lib fails to load, never block the tab
overview.primary_technology: SVG/Canvas via lightweight chart lib (recharts or visx — both already compatible with React 19 + Vite stack)

background_effects.description: flat dark surface, no animated background

particle_systems.description: not applicable to a finance reporting view

text_effects.description: numbers animate via count-up on first load (e.g. balance ticking to final value), text itself is static

cursor_effects.description: standard cursor, no custom effects (finance app, not showcase site)

canvas_drawings.description: donut chart (status/health), line/area chart (trend over time), horizontal bar chart (spend by category, mirrors Allure's Severity chart), histogram (transaction size distribution), horizontal progress bars (budget vs actual, mirrors Allure's Suite progress bars)
canvas_drawings.technology: recharts (SVG-based, tree-shakeable, React-idiomatic) — recommended over visx for faster implementation given no existing chart lib in WEB/package.json

params.animation_loop: one-shot entrance animation only, no continuous loop
params.color_scheme: semantic colors from design_system.color.semantic mapped to categories consistently across all charts
params.responsiveness: ResponsiveContainer, reflows to single column under 768px
params.interaction: hover tooltip + click to filter/drill down

svg_animations.description: donut/line chart stroke draws in on mount (recharts default animation)

visual_effects.composite_notes: This DNA intentionally scopes the Allure-dark aesthetic to the NEW Analytics tab only — the rest of the Volt app (yellow, light, mobile-card style) is untouched, per the user's decision to add this as an additional view rather than replace the existing dashboard. The two must still feel like the same product: Volt's yellow (#D4FF3D-class) accent color and existing Lucide icons carry across into the dark tab as the bridge, everything else (background, card surfaces, chart darkness) is new to this view only. No heavy visual effects (3D/shaders/particles) are appropriate for a financial reporting screen — the 'wow factor' Allure has comes from information density and color-coded clarity, not decoration, and that is what this DNA reproduces.
